FSLR.thesis_one_line: America's only scaled non-Chinese solar-panel maker, backed by a 45GW backlog and tax credits, priced as if its cash flow barely grows.
kill_criteria: Quarterly net sales YoY growth negative for two consecutive quarters (currently 1 of 2: Q2 2026)
Full-year 2026 guidance ($4.9-5.2bn sales / $2.6-2.8bn EBITDA) cut at any subsequent release
Contracted backlog falls below 40 GW (from 45.1 GW at 30-Jun-2026) without an offsetting new-bookings explanation
An adverse ruling or settlement in the securities class action or derivative suit that implies a material monetary liability or a restatement

Treasury guidance or legislative action that narrows the FEOC "material assistance" safe harbor in a way that disqualifies a material share of First Solar's supply chain from 45X eligibility before 2030
key_adverse_facts: New securities class action filed 23-Jun-2026 (E.D.N.Y.) alleging false statements about First Solar's ability to manage US tariff-policy impacts; shareholder derivative suit filed 28-Jul-2026 -- neither was in the original triage

Revenue growth turned negative in the most recent quarter (Q2 2026 net sales -3.7% YoY, attributed by the 10-Q to customer contract terminations; backlog 47.9 -> 45.1 GW) while gross margin rose to 57.3%, of which an $88.6m one-off net IEEPA tariff-refund benefit is the first-named driver (ex-item GM about 48.9%) [Corrected 2026-10-06, DVH4]

Section 45X credit for solar components carries new Foreign-Entity-of-Concern 'material assistance' restrictions (effective for tax years after 4-Jul-2025) and a 65% domestic-content threshold for 'integrated' components (after 31-Dec-2026) -- compliance risk not fully resolved

JinkoSolar patent litigation (stayed pending USITC Section 337 determination) and an unresolved Federal Circuit antidumping/countervailing-duty appeal leave some retroactive duty exposure legally open
data_conflicts: d4_live_snapshot freeCashflow ($1,598.7m TTM) is ~$99m (6.6%) above the SEC-XBRL-derived TTM FCF this dossier computes ($1,500.1m); immaterial to the thesis but d4's freeCashflow field should not be treated as primary for this name
Q2 2026 10-Q Note 9 shows total debt $37.6m (all current); d4's Yahoo total-debt field ($194.0m) is not supported, so net cash is about $1.69bn and EV about $17.41bn [Corrected 2026-10-06, DVH4]
FSLR.confidence_in_thesis: medium -- valuation and backlog evidence are strong, but two fresh, unresolved lawsuits and a policy-dependent margin structure are real, unquantified overhangs

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 systematic valuation exists for FSLR; this dossier is the first valuation view on file. DVH4 (2026-10-06) restated on the programme basis (Ke 11.34%, equity value, FCF after SBC): implied FCF growth +3.7%/yr vs base 6-8%; still below, but the gap is much narrower than the dossier's -1.0%/yr at 9.5%.

GEN.thesis_one_line: Cheap, deleveraged Norton/Avast/LifeLock cash cow with accelerating growth, but a fresh ~$12bn bid for GoDaddy makes the balance-sheet story unresolved.
kill_criteria: A signed, binding GoDaddy (or other >$5bn) acquisition agreement is announced without disclosed financing terms that keep pro-forma net debt/EBITDA under ~3.5x within 12 months
Net debt/EBITDA rises above 3.5x for any reason (deal-related or organic)
Quarterly organic revenue growth below 5% YoY for two consecutive quarters (current: accelerating, 11% last quarter)
FY27 guidance cut at any subsequent release (currently raised twice in the trailing year per the sources reviewed)
Buyback program suspended or materially reduced to fund M&A
key_adverse_facts: Preliminary ~$12bn takeover approach for GoDaddy reported 24-Sep-2026 (press-sourced, no confirming 8-K found in this pass); GEN shares fell ~12% on the news; any deal would likely require a large equity component given GEN's own ~$8bn net debt vs GoDaddy's ~$3.8bn debt -- this is exactly the kind of 'pending deal' the program's own sleeve-construction rules treat as an automatic exclusion for other names, and it broke one day before this dossier's data cutoff

GAAP operating margin has compressed from the low-40s% (mid-FY25) to the low-30s% (FY27) even as revenue accelerated, reflecting MoneyLion integration and $32m of restructuring plus $23m of litigation costs disclosed for Q1 FY27
A $900m 6.75% note matures 30-Sep-2027, inside the thesis horizon, competing for capital with whatever the GoDaddy situation ultimately requires
Legacy TCPA robocall class action settled for $9.95m (final approval 14-Jul-2026) -- resolved but confirms ongoing consumer-marketing legal risk
GEN.horizon: 12-36 months if the GoDaddy situation resolves without value-destructive financing; otherwise reassess
GEN.confidence_in_thesis: low -- the standalone valuation and growth case is high-confidence, but the unresolved M&A approach makes the near-term capital-structure outcome genuinely unknown

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 systematic valuation exists for GEN. Restated 2026-10-10 (DV18) on the programme basis: Ke 9.91% (5.17% + 1.144 x 4.14%), equity value $12.94bn, FCF after SBC about $1,308M: implied 10-year FCF growth is -2.6%/yr (original -0.4% on an EV basis at WACC 9%) against a +5-7% base: below. The standalone reverse DCF supports 'cheap', but the verdict is held at WATCH pending the GoDaddy situation, which valuation alone cannot resolve. Note: Q1 FY27 reported GAAP revenue growth was 6%; the 11% quoted is the non-GAAP comparable-basis rate.

KLAC.thesis_one_line: Best-moat semicap inspection-tools maker with real accelerating growth, but priced for decade-long growth this cyclical industry has never sustained.
kill_criteria: Quarterly revenue YoY growth below 5% for two consecutive quarters (currently accelerating at 7-15%)
GAAP diluted EPS guidance cut at any subsequent release (currently 2-for-2 met/beaten in this pass's sample)
China revenue share or absolute dollars fall further in a way the company attributes explicitly to new export restrictions
Net debt/EBITDA (currently trivial) rises above 1.0x without a value-accretive reason disclosed
Trailing P/FCF (corrected basis) stays above 50x for more than two quarters after revenue growth decelerates below 10% YoY
key_adverse_facts: Reverse DCF implies the market is pricing ~23.6%/yr (SBC treated as a cost; 22.5% before the DV25 correction) FCF growth for 10 years, versus an evidence-based base case of roughly 12-14%/yr -- a bar this cyclical industry has not cleared over any historical 10-year window, including the current AI-driven upswing

China export-control risk is reduced in relative weight (China revenue share fell from 42.8% FY2024 to 29.8% FY2026) but not resolved -- the FY2026 10-K attributes flat absolute China revenue to export controls offsetting legacy-node capex, meaning further tightening could still cut dollars, not just share
Trailing P/FCF is ~65x on the corrected (primary-sourced) FCF figure -- the stock is priced overwhelmingly on future growth, not current cash generation

KLA does not tag a discrete GAAP OperatingIncomeLoss line in recent XBRL; operating-margin figures in this dossier are taken from earnings-release text, not derived from machine-readable filings -- a minor sourcing friction
data_conflicts: d4_live_snapshot's forward-estimate-trend fields for KLAC (eps_q0, eps_q1, eps_fy0, eps_fy1, rev_q0, rev_fy0, rev_fy1, and derived multiples pe_fy0/pe_fy1/pe_ntm_qsum) are internally inconsistent with the row's own headline fields and with primary SEC data (e.g. rev_fy0 = $5.04bn vs actual ~$13.6-14bn annual revenue; eps_fy0/eps_fy1 of $17.49/$23.19 vs SEC-confirmed post-split trailing EPS of ~$3.66-3.70) -- likely a stale pre-split pull or symbol-mapping fault specific to KLAC, not corrected in d4 itself given this agent's write-scope limits; flagged for DA follow-up

d4_live_snapshot / Yahoo freeCashflow TTM ($2,625m) understates the SEC-primary-sourced TTM FCF ($3,767.1m, from FY2026 10-K operating cash flow $4,143.1m minus capex $375.9m) by roughly 30% ($1.14bn) -- the largest data conflict found across this batch, since it feeds directly into the quant model's FCF-yield (Value family) score
KLAC.confidence_in_thesis: high -- the business-quality and growth evidence is unusually strong and internally consistent; the valuation conclusion (priced above a defensible base case) is the source of the WATCH verdict, not doubt about the business
